## Design

### 2026-10-07 – I spent about two hours today getting up to speed with KiCad, and in the process, I completely finished the schematic for my Starbie project.

**2h**

I spent about two hours today getting up to speed with KiCad, and in the process, I completely finished the schematic for my Starbie project.

First, I downloaded the "Care Package" ZIP file and extracted the symbol and footprint libraries. Since I had never imported footprints into KiCad before, I quickly checked a YouTube tutorial to see how to correctly install the .sym files and .pretty footprint folders.

Once KiCad was configured, I opened the schematic editor to place all the components for the board. I added the XIAO-ESP32-C3 microcontroller, connected push-buttons, and set up the power connections for +5V, +3.3V, and GND using power symbols and net labels. Connecting components via net labels made the workspace much cleaner, as I didn't have to draw physical traces all across the screen.
![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 9.02.51 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wQyLGXeMuFuhPsJ7zdLWERYOByDhKh2B/ca8eeb4fcfca98c2f20d4717ac1f7890ef9ac28a71c3365a547cb10b63710345.png)
After the basic circuit was in place, I wired up the external modules. I added a 4-pin header for the OLED display, an 8-pin header for the MPU6050 motion sensor, and the DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor. Once all connections were made, I opened the footprint assignment tool to map each schematic symbol to its corresponding physical component layout—following the instructions provided in the project files.

Everything saved without issues, and the schematic is now fuly complete!. Next is moving to the PCB editor to design the physical board layout and route all the traces. I will do this tomorrow.

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 9.03.27 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wQyLGXeMuFuhPsJ7zdLWERYOByDhKh2B/82e929d986d1b680cd03c039892c2f2112e783170e3d94f50064c7d386ad941f.png)

### 2026-10-08 – today was the second day since i have started work on this project, and I spent about 2.5 hours working on the physical board design in KiCad.

**3h**

today was the second day since i have started work on this project, and I spent about 2.5 hours working on the physical board design in KiCad.
I began by opening the PCB editor and importing all the elements from the previous day’s work using the "Update PCB from schematic" function.
Since the components were initially scattered randomly across the screen, the first step was to determine their placement. I watched a brief video on youtube to learn how to draw a custom board outline on the Edge Cuts layer. And then I carefully positioned the ESP32  board, the oled display headers, the 2 sensors & the pushbuttons within these boundaries to create a logical layout. I also didnt like the somewhat pixelated outline of the guide project so i instead spent an absurd amount of time getting the shape right (Still not perfect tho)

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 at 7.47.52 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wQyLGXeMuFuhPsJ7zdLWERYOByDhKh2B/faca43866cb0b5794a3b020daa61d30e95cc9726f681909000bc5a2ec5a36ee8.png)

Routing the connections proved to be somewhat more challenging than expected. I toggled between the top and bottom layers of the board using the "X" key to connect all the pads. I also added a GND planeacross the entire board after watching the  short youtube  tutorial linked in the guide on how filled zones work.
(The tutorial was super helpful at places and a bit too brief at others, i found youtube to be a great help wherever the tutorial skipped a few things)
The Design Rule Check  initially returned a few rather confusing error messages.

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 at 7.54.00 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wQyLGXeMuFuhPsJ7zdLWERYOByDhKh2B/47dffb228879ef0d82ecea363f18bafd1b1fb7c89f18242e2eebbd350f213254.png)

 I spent a lot of time fixing missing trace connections and correcting overlapping traces until the checks passed. Once  drc showed no errors, except error J1, my work for the day was done

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 at 7.47.35 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wQyLGXeMuFuhPsJ7zdLWERYOByDhKh2B/1201c15feb0fe4c7da46d0b6f00d88e695c046a4eca2d55e749b4797b42fcb03.png)
i am planning to add some cool pokemon vibe inspired graphics ane logos to the board tomorrow
